abstract: Cell size is an important functional attribute of single-celled organisms, and whole genome duplication (WGD) has long been hypothesized to double the volume of unicells. Pollen of flowering plants is effectively a single-celled organism, comprising the "vegetative cell" of the male gametophyte, which carries the male germline (two sperm cells or their precursor) within its cytoplasm. Instantaneous doubling of evolved pollen size is likely to be excessive, which should bias evolution in young polyploids to size reduction. Here, I test the hypotheses that the magnitude of the effect of WGD on pollen diameter should be doubled volume at inception, and less-than-doubled volume in evolved autotetraploids. Taking data from the literature, I compared 1n = 2x to 1n = 1x pollen diameters in 286 pairs of intraspecific autotetraploids and their diploid progenitors at four successive evolutionary ages: 1) diploid anthers producing some non-reduced pollen, 2) newly formed synthetic or spontaneous autotetraploids, 3) established autotetraploid cultivars, and 4) wild intraspecific autotetraploid cytotypes. Relative to 1x pollen, the volume of 2x non-reduced pollen was at least doubled at inception (31 species), doubled in 65 synthetic and 34 old cultivars, and on average 46% smaller-than-doubled in 54 wild autotetraploid species. Neither 1x pollen size nor 1Cx DNA content of diploids affected the results. Furthermore, wind- versus animal-pollination had little effect. Finally, in 16 autotetraploid-diploid pairs, the differences in pollen size were not correlated with the differences in their 1Cx DNA content. In sum, WGD doubles pollen volume and doubled volume persists in cultivars maintained in benign conditions, but over time in natural conditions, pollen of wild autotetraploids is strongly biased towards reversion to progenitor sizes. Since pollen downsizing after WGD was not matched by genome downsizing, pollen size reduction in young autotetraploids must largely evolve by gene regulation and expression, rather than by a direct relationship between genome size or gene dosage and cell size.
